Elaine: Heads-up — customer on Dedicated started seeing intermittent 401s and a surge in billing after we regenerated clients against the updated OpenAPI spec. Repro + logs below.

Matt: Oof. Which SDK versions did they pick up?

Elaine: They upgraded to redwood-python-client v1.12.0 and @redwood/ts-client v0.9.4 (both generated from latest spec). Previously on py v1.10.3 and ts v0.8.9.

Liam: Can you paste a minimal failing curl or code sample from their logs?

Elaine: From their logs (token redacted):
```
curl -i -X POST https://dedicated.us.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-13b", "input":"hi"}'
```
Server returns 401 roughly half the time. When it succeeds, response is normal. They also show many client-side retries within 10s windows.

Yoav: Intermittent 401 + retries = either auth header sometimes missing/renamed or gateway misclassifying failures. Any header diffs between successful and failed requests?

Elaine: Yes — good catch. In the SDK request dumps, failing requests include an extra header: `Organization: org-123` (Titlecase). Successful requests either omit this header or send `X-Organization-Id: org-123`.

Anita: That matches a recent spec change. The OpenAPI entry for org headers was renamed from `x-organization-id` to `organization`. Our TypeScript generator maps that to `Organization` (exact param name), but the gateway expects `x-organization-id`. So unknown header -> gateway treats request as missing org -> token rejected -> 401.

Matt: So two root causes: the spec rename produced a header-name mismatch, and the regenerated clients have a more aggressive retry policy that retries on 401s, amplifying billing. Can we confirm where retry-on-401 came from?

Liam: I inspected gen-templates: a change in the common retry policy toggled retry-on-401 to true in the default client behavior earlier this month. The intent was to smooth transient auth flakiness, but here it makes repeated attempts after a header mismatch.

Elaine: Repro steps I gave the customer (short):
1) pip install redwood-python-client==1.12.0
2) npm i @redwood/ts-client@0.9.4
3) run this python snippet repeatedly until a 401 appears (~50% they saw):
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
c = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED", org_id="org-123")
print(c.generate("hi"))
```

Yoav: Short-term mitigations: pin customers to previous client versions (py 1.10.x / ts 0.8.x); set env or config to disable retry-on-401 if exposed; or add a temporary gateway compatibility layer that accepts `Organization` and maps it to `X-Organization-Id`.

Anita: I'm opening a template PR to revert the retry-on-401 default and to add a mapping for header names in generated clients. Will also add unit tests asserting header emission. Expect a 1-2 day turnaround for template + hotfix client releases.

Matt: Who changed the OpenAPI file? Need the spec PR for audit and release notes.

Liam: Spec PR #342 (infra-team) on 2026-03-01 renamed the header param to `organization`. We missed adding a generator mapping to preserve `x-organization-id` for compatibility.

Elaine: Support reply outline I prepared:
- Root cause: OpenAPI header rename + client template change (header name + retry policy).
- Immediate: pin to previous versions or set RETRY_ON_401=false if possible; gateway compat will be enabled shortly.
- Medium: release hotfix clients (1.12.1 and 0.9.5) reverting retry default and fixing header mapping.
- Long-term: add CI e2e regen test that validates header names and retry flags after client generation.

Yoav: I'll deploy a short-lived gateway shim to accept both `Organization` and `X-Organization-Id` so tokens aren't rejected while clients roll.

Anita: Bisecting generator commits to find when Titlecase header emission landed. Opening PR now.

devex-bot: created task -> #task/regen-client-hotfix (assignee: anita)

Anita: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/gen-templates/pull/389 -- reverts retry-on-401 default, adds header-name mapping, and unit tests.

Matt: After we ship hotfix clients, outreach to customers who upgraded so we can help them pin/migrate.

Elaine: I'll update the customer with the pin + temporary mitigations and keep support looped in. Closing here after releases are out. :thumbsup:
